## Darkroom

Darkroom is a self-hosted service that brings a household's photos together on Unraid: each person's iPhone originals (backed up to Immich by Immich's own app, then copied once onto Unraid), the extras that exist only in Google Photos (pulled from Takeout exports by a browser worker), and one Immich library per person. Photos are cleared off the iPhones only once they exist on Unraid and in Google. Python backend in `darkroom/` (`server/` the HTTP handler and route table, `domain/` the dedupe, eligibility and ingest pipeline, `providers/` exiftool and Immich, `storage/` the database and the folder tree), the browser worker in `darkroom_browser/`, the Svelte web app in `frontend/`, the design in `docs/SPEC.md`. The one thing that can lose a photo is deleting it from a phone: read `AGENTS.md`'s "Darkroom's promises" first, then `SECURITY.md`, and treat any change near eligibility, cleanup, dedupe decisions or a file under a person's `originals/` as the riskiest kind.

## Private data here

Private data is anything from a real household: a person's name, an email address, a Google account id, a device name, an archive or export id, a photo's path or file name, GPS coordinates, the capture time of a real photo, a real Takeout export, a session, device or worker token, an API key or `DARKROOM_SECRET_KEY`. It would land in a test, a fixture, a sample export, a screenshot, an issue or pull request text, a log line or an error message. Every fixture is generated and made up: `tests/takeout_fixtures.py` builds synthetic Takeout exports, `tests/fixtures/media.py` makes the media files, `tests/privacy.py` holds the canary values logs are checked against (`no_leaks`). A real-looking name, email, place, file name, export or token beside them is a blocking finding. The repository is public, and the rule is the same as in Waypoint and Runway: nothing of anyone's photos or Google data belongs in it.

## Generated files and the checks that cover them

`docs/openapi.json` and `frontend/src/lib/api-types.ts` are generated by `tools/api_contract.py` from the route table and the handlers' annotations, and `docs/feature-map.json` by `tools/feature_map.py`; CI's "CI / checks" job fails when either is stale, so they are left out of `diff.patch` and only listed. `poetry.lock` and `frontend/package-lock.json` are covered by the installs in CI and by `pip-audit` and `npm audit`. `.semgrep/examples/` holds deliberate rule violations for `.semgrep/check_examples.py`: a finding there is expected, a change to the rules or the examples is not generated and is read in full.

## What matters most in AGENTS.md

"Darkroom's promises" (an original is written once; dedupe deletes nothing on Unraid; a photo is eligible for deletion from an iPhone only on the stated rules, re-checked right before deleting; the browser worker never types a Google password or 2FA code; metadata gaps are XMP sidecars, never rewritten media; no design ships without sign-off), the "Conventions" (one paved path: outbound HTTP through `darkroom/tls.py`, subprocesses only in `darkroom/providers/exiftool.py`, request bodies through `darkroom/validate.py`, time through `darkroom/dates.py`; every route declares its auth kind in `darkroom/server/routes.py`; no comments or docstrings; a schema change has a migration with its test) and "Mistakes that keep coming back", whose bold titles are the `kind` of each finding. `SECURITY.md` says who may call which route and that secrets are never committed, logged or returned.
